content: New data from outsourcing firm Tussell shows UK public bodies paid £3.4bn to private consultants last year, a 62% rise since 2019-20, with spending remaining elevated since Covid rather than returning to earlier levels. This highlights the scale of the task for Keir Starmer’s government, which has pledged to halve such spending. Since Labour took office, almost £650m in fresh consultancy contracts have been signed, including a KPMG deal worth up to £223m to train civil servants. Labour peer and finance academic Prem Sikka criticised the heavy reliance on consultants as “scandalous,” arguing they add limited value given the complexity of government organisations.
